releases.notes:
##  Additions
* Added `SerializableDataType#validateValue` method, used for validating the type the data type operates on (if it implements the `Validatable` interface)

##  Changes
* Deprecated `SimpleDataObjectFactory` in favor of using `DataObjectFactory` directly via `DataObjectFactory#simple`
* Renamed `SerializableDataTypeList` class to `ListSerializableDataType`
* Renamed `FunctionedFieldImpl` class to `FunctionedDefaultFieldImpl`
* Renamed `OptionalFieldImpl` class to `DefaultedFieldImpl`
* Renamed `Field#path` method to `Field#name`
* Tweaked field presence check logic in `SerializableData$Instance` to ensure that the default value of fields are only checked if the field doesn't have any defined value
* Separated setting of defaulted and functioned default fields of `SerializableData$Instance` (when decoding) to avoid nullability issues functioned default fields relying on defaulted fields

mods.name: Calio
mods.description: A simple library mod, mainly adds a serializable data system.

releases.notes:
##  Additions
* Added helper methods for wrapping data types in an optional;
  * `SerializableDataType#optional`; for strict optionals.
  * `SerializableDataType#lenientOptional`; for lenient optionals, where the data type will return `Optional#empty` if it errors.
  * `SerializableDataType#lenientOptional(Consumer<String>)`; for lenient optionals with custom error handling.
* Added `RECIPE_SERIALIZER` data type.
* Added `RECIPE` data type that actually corresponds to a `Recipe<?>`.
* Added `RECIPE_ENTRY` data type that corresponds to a `RecipeEntry<?>`.

##  Changes
* `StrictCodec<T>` interface no longer exists in favor of simplicity.
* `SerializableDataType<T>` no longer implements `Codec<T>`. To decode/encode an object, you can use any of the following methods:
  * `SerializableDataType#codec`; for querying the data type's `Codec<T>`.
  * `SerializableDataType#read(DynamicOps<T>, I)`; for decoding a `DataResult<T>` from `I` (the input) using `DynamicOps<I>`, where `T` is the data type's type and `I` being the type to decode `T` from.
  * `SerializableDaType#write(DynamicOps<I>, T)`; for encoding a `T` into a `DataResult<I>` using `DynamicOps<T>`, where `T` is the data type's type and `I` being the type to encode `T` to.

##  Fixes
* Fixed `eat_seconds` parameter of `SerializableDataTypes#FOOD_COMPONENT` accepting a non-zero positive floating point value instead of non-negative floating point value.
* Fixed `SerializableDataType#INGREDIENT` unable to be synced to the client.
* Fixed enum data types (e.g: using `SerializableDataType#enumValue`) case-sensitivity when checking for matching additional values.

releases.notes:
##  Changes
* Made the `SerializableDataTypes#RECIPE` data type use `Recipe#CODEC` when parsing from/to packet byte buffer and JSON.
* Simplified how resources are collected in Calio's custom JSON data loaders.
* Renamed `CalioJsonDataLoader` to `ExtendedJsonDataLoader`.
* Changed the key-value structure of `MultiJsonDataContainer`; it's now a `Map<String, Map<Identifier, List<JsonElement>>` (was previously `Map<Identifier, Map<String, List<JsonElement>>`.)

##  Additions
* Added `IExtendedJsonDataLoader` interface, which is implemented for most of the custom JSON data loaders. It adds two methods:
  * `ExtendedJsonDataLoader#onReject(String, Identifier)` for handling prepared data being rejected due to its resource conditions not fulfilled.
  * `ExtendedJsonDataLoader#onError(String, Identifier, String, Exception)` for handling errors while preparing data.
* Added `DataObjectRegistry$Builder#dataErrorHandler(TriConsumer<Identifier, String, Exception>)` for handling errors including the data pack's name.
* Added `DataObjectRegistry$Builder#dependencies(Identifier...)` for declaring the dependencies of the loader for the data object registry.
* Added `DataObjectRegistry$Builder#resourceType(ResourceType)` for specifying the resource type of the loader for the data object registry; optional.

##  Fixes
* Fixed `SerializableDataTypes#RECIPE` data type leniently parsing the recipe's ID and the recipe serializer's ID.

releases.notes:
## Changes
* Made registry key data types validate. This ensures that the element referenced by the serialized registry key exists to prevent potential crashes (e.g: via referencing a non-existent dimension, or damage type)
* Made tag data types validate. This ensures that the serialized tag of a registry exists to prevent potential crashes (e.g: via referencing a non-existent block tag)
* Made tag-like data types validate. This ensures that the specified IDs either reference an existing element or tag from a registry to prevent potential crashes (e.g: via referencing a non-existent entity type/entity type tag)

### Full changelog: [`v1.13.0...v1.13.1`](https://github.com/apace100/calio/compare/v1.13.0...v1.13.1)

## Additions
* Added `CalioJsonDataLoader`; similar to Minecraft's `JsonDataLoader`, except it supports JSONC/JSON5.

## Changes
* Added support for `*` (current namespace/path) to tag-like data type.
* Added methods to tag-like data type for clearing all its tags/entries and adding all the tags/entries of another tag-like.
* The item stack from the item stack data type is now instantiated using the specified item's default stack getter.

## Fixes
* Functioned default data fields in a serializable data are now written/read to/from buffers properly.
* Presence check of functioned default data fields from a serializable data is now done properly.

releases.notes:
* Added `TagLike<T>` class and data types for `TagLike<Block>`, `TagLike<Item>` and `TagLike<EntityType<?>>`.

A `TagLike<T>` is a collection of tags and elements of a certain type `T`. Using this data type allows creation of something akin to the `values` field in tags, hence the name `TagLike`. This means a `TagLike` is an array of IDs for elements, or IDs for tags when prepended with a `#`.

For example
```json
[
  "minecraft:stone",
  "minecraft:oak_leaves",
  "#minecraft:logs"
]
```
would be a valid value for a `TagLike<Block>` field.
